title: Content Delivery Networks (CDN)
definition: A CDN is a geographically distributed group of servers that work together to provide fast delivery of Internet content. By caching static assets (HTML, CSS, JS, Images) at edge nodes close to users, CDNs drastically reduce latency and server load.
simpleExplanation: Instead of shipping a pizza from New York to Tokyo, a CDN builds a pizza shop in Tokyo so the customer gets it fresh and fast.

rows: You upload content directly to the CDN. Best for large, static files.
CDN fetches from your origin server on the first request and caches it. Best for web traffic.

answers.question: Define Content Delivery Networks.
answers.answer: Content Delivery Networks is a core mechanism in frontend architectures.

answers.question: What is the main bottleneck for Content Delivery Networks?
answers.answer: Usually network latency or CPU-bound synchronous tasks blocking the main thread.
